targetText: Our answer is that antagonism is one form, but not the only form, of the struggle of opposites.
explanation: Not all conflicts are hostile fights to the death. Some conflicts are non-antagonistic and can be resolved peacefully. Real-life example: Roommates negotiating how to divide household chores is a non-antagonistic conflict; an intruder breaking in to steal your belongings is an antagonistic conflict.

targetText: Contradiction and struggle are universal and absolute, but the methods of resolving contradictions, that is, the forms of struggle, differ according to the differences in the nature of the contradictions.
explanation: Because conflicts vary in nature, your method of solving them must fit the situation. Real-life example: Differences of opinion among project teammates are resolved through discussion, while structural wage theft requires collective union action or legal pressure.

targetText: Lenin said, "Antagonism and contradiction are not at all one and the same. Under socialism, the first will disappear, the second will remain."
explanation: Lenin points out that even in a fair society without exploitation, people will still face challenges, decisions, and debates that drive progress. Real-life example: Even in a close-knit family, members will disagree on house design or budgeting, but those problems are solved through discussion rather than hostility.
